cea6858d5b9d2e2d: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals.

The all-stock deal, announced on Monday, will see Zscaler shareholders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for every share they own, representing a 34 percent premium on Friday's closing price. The transaction dwarfs even Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security upstart Wiz.

Buying Zscaler gives CrowdStrike a sizeable foothold in the network security market, where it will be going up against the likes of Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. The plan is to combine Falcon's endpoint protection capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security technology, giving customers a single platform for securing devices and the connections between them.

Naturally, there's an AI angle to the biggest cyber deal in history. CrowdStrike reckons owning both technologies will allow it to keep tabs on what AI agents are doing on corporate devices, where they're connecting, and what data they're getting their hands on.
CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described the proposed combination as "cybersecurity’s operating system."

The acquisition also gives CrowdStrike's salespeople plenty to get excited about. Around 8,000 Zscaler customers don't currently buy CrowdStrike's wares, and the companies already have more than 2,000 customers in common. CrowdStrike reckons it can boost its annualized revenue by around $1 billion within 30 months of closing the deal by selling more products to the two companies' existing customers.

Some of those customers, however, don't sound particularly keen on being cross-sold to. Over on Reddit's r/sysadmin subreddit, news of the purchase was met with a familiar set of concerns from IT professionals who've lived through big-ticket enterprise software acquisitions before.
"As a zscaler customer, this does worry me. Cost increase, forced move to Falcon, integration issues, etc," wrote one sysadmin.
Another, whose organization already uses both vendors' products, added: "I think they're both great products but I imagine they'll jack up the price for our next renewal. Fun."

CrowdStrike intends to make Zscaler's products available through its Falcon Flex licensing scheme, which allows customers to commit to a certain level of spending and pick and choose the products they deploy. Monday's acquisition announcement didn't spell out what the deal would mean for customers who want to continue using Zscaler alongside a rival endpoint security product.

Others raised concerns about the fate of Red Canary, the managed detection and response specialist snapped up by Zscaler in August 2025. CrowdStrike already operates a competing service in Falcon Complete.

There may also be some nervous employees at both companies. CrowdStrike is targeting $500 million in annual cost savings within two years of completing the acquisition, identifying datacenter infrastructure, supplier spending, and wider operations as areas where it can trim the fat. Neither company disclosed whether that would involve job cuts.

Then there's the matter of putting more of the world's corporate security infrastructure in the hands of CrowdStrike, whose botched July 2024 software update took down an estimated 8.5 million Windows machines, grounding flights and disrupting hospitals, banks, and businesses worldwide. The incident gave IT departments a rather painful lesson in the risks of relying heavily on a single technology supplier.

The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, assuming regulators and Zscaler shareholders give it the green light. Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry will remain in charge of the business and take a seat on CrowdStrike's board.

CrowdStrike reckons the combined business will have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue when the deal closes. Judging by the reaction from some customers, they'll be keeping a particularly close eye on how much of that revenue comes from them. ®

c0f7df7687882154: LONDON: US stock futures and European shares came under pressure on Tuesday as the early euphoria following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded, with investors cautious about further AI-driven gains and upcoming US inflation data.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.1%, weighed down by a sharp drop in mining stocks.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.
However, it also left unanswered questions over Huang, who had resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.
"With Jensen's return, it assures people massively and gives hope that the data centre construction continues and that boosts US GDP," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst, IG Group in London.

"But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly. What did he know? What else did he do? How much went to China? And these questions will continue to chip away at market confidence," Beauchamp said.
Nvidia's shares fell nearly 4% in US premarket trading, a day after marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly US$1 trillion in value to the company.
In Asia, Taiwanese shares shot up 9% from an eight-month low, with Nvidia's primary contract chip manufacturer TSMC and assembler Foxconn both nearly 10% higher at their daily limits.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed nearly 4%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and recording its biggest single-day gain since July 31.

"By the end of the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors' expectations. My point is: Jensen's return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion," Glenn Yin, director of research at online trading platform ACCM, told the Reuters Global Markets Forum.
Chinese shares were an exception to the relief rally, making only small gains due to concerns that tighter curbs on the exports of US chips are in the works.
Dollar, yields await inflation data

New York Federal Reserve president John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest-rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the US central bank's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersised 50-basis-point increase is around 5%.
The US dollar index eased slightly from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.
The sharp AI rebound has eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening.
The yield on the benchmark US 2-year Treasury note edged up for a second day and was last at 4.6684%, while the yield on the 10-year note edged lower to 4.9197%.
Brent crude futures dipped to US$88.75 a barrel, near a three-month low, on rising supplies from the Middle East.
Spot gold fell to US$3,619.70 per ounce. Copper, a key material used in data-centre infrastructure, retreated 3% after jumping 5% on Monday.

ffac2711f310feed: LONDON, Nov 24 — More than 5,000 deaths were linked to heat in England this year, the highest since records began in 2016, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said today PA Media/dpa reported.
An estimated 5,258 deaths were associated with hot weather in 2026, comfortably beating the previous high of 2,985 set in 2022.

The year saw the United Kingdom experience its warmest summer on record, with parts of the country enduring multiple heatwaves over several months, beginning in late May when temperatures peaked at 35.1 degrees Celsius in London, an all-time high for the month.
A heatwave at the end of June prompted a rare red alert from the Met Office for extreme heat and saw temperatures reach 38.0 degrees on June 26 in Norfolk, another new monthly record.
As the scorching summer continued, England saw its driest July since data began, with only 7mm of rain measured, or 10 per cent of the long-term average.
A heatwave in mid-August saw temperatures climb as high as 38.2 degrees in Gloucestershire, making it the hottest day of the year.
In its report, the UKHSA said: “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer with the highest mortality observed since 2016 when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports.
“Significant mortality impacts were observed early in the summer season, with over 3,000 estimated heat-associated deaths across the May and June heat episodes.”
The highest number of heat-associated deaths were recorded between June 21 and 28, when an estimated 2,401 deaths were linked to this period of extreme heat.
This year’s total of 5,258 deaths follows a run of much lower annual totals, with 2,295 in 2023, 1,311 in 2024 and 1,504 in 2025.

The report said intense heat early in the summer season “can pose particular risks as unusually hot weather may occur before people, communities and services have fully prepared and are ready to respond to hot weather conditions”.

It added: “These findings therefore reinforce the importance of heat-health preparedness measures being in place from the start of the season, rather than focusing solely on the warmest periods of mid-summer.”

Dr Ross Thompson, principal environmental health scientist at the UKHSA, said: “Heat can affect anyone, but older adults, young children, pregnant women and people with underlying health conditions are at greater risk.
“Climate change is already affecting people’s health in England, and as the climate continues to warm we can expect periods of extreme heat to become longer, more frequent and more intense.
“That is why it is vital that individuals, communities, health and care services and local organisations are prepared, not just during a heatwave but in the longer term.
“The decisions we make now will shape the health impacts people experience in the decades ahead.” — Bernama

fbc9f17566894033: The European Commission has confirmed that hackers made off with personal data in the AI-assisted cyberattack disclosed last week, but has relied on a website notice rather than contacting affected users directly.

Speaking at a press briefing on Monday, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed that EU Academy, an online learning platform offering courses on EU policies and initiatives, was among the systems compromised during the cyber campaign targeting the bloc's executive arm.

The stolen data includes the names and email addresses of people outside the EU institutions, though the Commission has yet to figure out how many users are affected or whether other personal information was compromised. Public access to the platform has been disabled as a precaution.

Despite confirming the theft, the Commission hasn't contacted affected individuals directly. Instead, it has posted a notice on the EU Academy website, a decision Regnier defended when quizzed by reporters on Monday.
"There was no reach out to individual users, but rather a general message to all users on the website out of transparency," Regnier said.

The notice warns users that they could find themselves on the receiving end of spearphishing attacks, impersonation attempts, and spam as a result of the breach. The Commission is also advising users not to hand over personal information to anyone who contacts them claiming to be involved in EU Academy activities.

The trouble with notifying users via the EU Academy website is that they've already been told not to come back until January. A separate notice says the platform will be offline from November 11 through January 14, 2027, while the Commission rebuilds it. When it reopens, users will have to register again, and any record of their previous coursework won't be transferred.
The Register has asked the Commission whether the downtime and the requirement to create new accounts are connected to the cyberattack.A spokesperson didn't answer those points.
The Commission has informed the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS), the watchdog responsible for policing EU institutions' handling of personal data.
The EDPS told The Register that the Commission had notified it of the incident in stages, but declined to say whether it considered the Commission's approach to notifying affected users sufficient.

"I can confirm that the EDPS has been informed and notified in phases by the European Commission," a spokesperson said. "Our colleagues remain in regular contact with EC services on the cyberattack and its implication. This is an ongoing case, so I cannot tell you more at this stage on the actions the EDPS might take as supervisory authority."

The Commission first publicly acknowledged the cyberattack last Thursday, almost a month after suspicious activity was detected on October 22. Several internal applications were temporarily taken offline, and while most had since been restored, some remained unavailable at the time of Thursday's briefing.

The Commission has confirmed the attackers used an AI-assisted hacking tool, and the incident comes amid mounting concerns over ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework that security researchers have linked to large-scale cyber espionage campaigns.
More than a month after the Commission first spotted the intrusion, Regnier was unwilling to say on Monday whether its security teams had finally seen off the hackers.
"As long as the investigation is ongoing, I will not make any conclusive statements at this stage on where we are," he said. ®

7991d6a9c1a6b8b6: THE HAGUE: Jaguar Land Rover said Monday that it would "protect" its intellectual property after a Dutch court halted the sale of an SUV by the Chinese automaker BYD in the European Union, saying it copies too closely the iconic Land Rover Defender.

A district court in The Hague found that BYD's Ti 7 model has distinctive and protected elements of the Defender L663 design, notably the curved "shoulders" of the bodywork as well as the rounded corners, wheel arches and the vehicle's overall silhouette.
National European courts can issue intellectual property rulings that apply throughout the EU when the products in question are sold across the 27-nation bloc.
"JLR continues to invest in creativity and innovation. We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary," a Jaguar spokesperson told AFP.
"Legal proceedings are ongoing and we won't be commenting further at this time."
BYD said it would appeal Friday's ruling, which temporarily prohibits the Chinese electric vehicle specialist from importing, manufacturing, stocking or selling the Ti 7 across the European Union.
Shares in BYD slipped in Hong Kong on Monday following the ruling.
"BYD strongly disagrees with today's judgment and will appeal it. The BYD Ti 7 is the result of BYD's own independent design work and infringes none of JLR's rights," the company said in a statement.

50dc6ec5c93f6b80: A software fault cut short BepiColombo's Mercury orbit insertion burn, but the European Space Agency (ESA) says the mission remains on track to separate its two science orbiters on December 9.

ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), still carrying JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (Mio), fired its four axial thrusters on November 21 to place the spacecraft in orbit. The burn began at 1824 UTC, when BepiColombo was approximately 635 km above the planet's surface. It was supposed to last for 37 minutes but shut down early.
The shutdown, caused by a software issue involving attitude guidance and thruster control, left the spacecraft in safe mode, a protective state in which all non-essential activities cease.
Ignacio Tanco, ESA's BepiColombo Flight Operations Director, said: "Upon finding Bepi in safe mode, it was like flipping a switch. Everybody was focused in understanding what had happened."
The burn achieved around 77 percent of the planned velocity change, securing an orbit around Mercury but leaving BepiColombo taking 75 hours to circle the planet instead of the intended 58.

The good news is that multiple burns were always going to be needed to adjust the orbit ahead of Mio separation and MPO reaching its science orbit. "The remaining MOI [Mercury Orbit Insertion] sequence has already been adapted to the new trajectory, with no additional burns required," ESA said.
"After each burn, the Flight Dynamics team determines the achieved orbit to then design the next manoeuvre," said Frank Budnik, ESA's BepiColombo Flight Dynamics Manager.

"So, the sequence is not only more propellant-efficient, it also allows Flight Dynamics to adapt each subsequent burn to the spacecraft's actual trajectory. It's a dynamic sequence! Each new manoeuvre is based on the previous ones."
Teams at ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) and Airbus continue to investigate the underlying software fault.
ESA has not said whether the revised burn sequence will affect propellant reserves available for a possible mission extension.
The separation of Mio and MPO is planned for December 9, and more burns will be needed to guide MPO to its final orbit by March 2027, with science operations starting in April 2027. ®

84edfb5a38475599: One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.

xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.

As of October 2026, data center developers have announced plans for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.

It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.

Building your own power plant is generally more expensive than just hooking up to the grid, but the AI rush has made developers willing to pay a significant premium to get online faster. “The biggest motivator for on-site power right now from data centers is speed,” says Musfika Mishi, an associate at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.

When developers want to build a new industrial facility—like a data center—that requires a lot of electricity, they need to request a grid connection from a local utility or regional grid operator. That request kicks off a yearslong process in which grid planners study the existing grid to understand what would need to be built to safely deliver power to the facility without compromising reliability. Upgrades might be required, like building new transmission lines or larger transformers, and the developer might be on the hook to help pay for them.

Rather than waiting for that process to play out, developers can opt to instead build their own power plants. These facilities are referred to as “behind the meter” because they sit on the customer’s side of a utility meter—supplying the building directly, rather than relying on a utility via a grid hookup.

“This shift in the data center developers’ power strategies towards off-grid gas raises some important questions about how data centers will be powered going forward,” says Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at the think tank Energy Innovation.

Behind-the-meter doesn’t always mean being totally disconnected from the grid, however. Some facilities may build such plants as a temporary measure, eventually connecting to the grid and tapping their own power plants only as backup. “It’s really just a very expensive way to bridge that maybe five-to-seven-year timeline gap until these data centers can get a grid connection,” Pierpont says.

Even if gas plants are pitched as a near-term solution, building new fossil fuel infrastructure could lead to longer-term effects, since an operator might choose to continue running plants once they’ve spent money building them. “Even though data centers say that it’s a grid-bridging solution, the probability that it is going to be in use much longer is a real risk, and that leads to fossil fuel lock-in,” Mishi says.

The on-site gas rush could have major implications for greenhouse-gas emissions. Today, the US grid is still reliant on fossil fuels, but nuclear and renewables together make up about 40% of electricity generation. That means making a grid connection is generally a lower-emissions option than relying entirely on an on-site gas plant. (That’s not the case everywhere—India, for example, is expecting to see a data center boom in the next decade, and its grid is largely served by emissions-intensive coal-fired power plants today.)

Utilities are already planning to build more natural gas power plants on the grid to meet rising electricity demand. Equipment manufacturers are struggling to keep up with the surge, and it’s pushing developers of behind-the-meter plants toward less-efficient alternatives.

Today, large natural gas plants generally use combined-cycle turbines. These capture heat to generate additional electricity, making them more efficient than single-cycle turbines, which are generally cheaper to build. Very few of the planned behind-the-meter facilities, however, will use combined-cycle turbines, Mishi says. That means these off-grid plants will likely produce more greenhouse-gas emissions than even other natural gas resources.

BloombergNEF is also tracking on-site natural gas plants at data centers, finding 181 gigawatts’ worth of announced projects globally, with 90% of that capacity designated for the US. If all planned behind-the-meter gas plants for data centers in the US go ahead, they could emit 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent each year by 2035, according to a BloombergNEF report. That’s 152 million metric tons more than if those data centers pulled power from the US grid—a difference greater than the total annual emissions of the Netherlands.

And while it might seem logical that data centers bringing their own power could ease communities’ energy bills, those facilities going off-grid doesn’t protect prices for everyone else, says Matthias Fripp, director of global policy research at Energy Innovation. More demand for natural gas could push its price higher, he explains, which could in turn raise rates for the roughly 60% of American households that use natural gas for heating and cooking. That effect may also trickle into electricity prices.

There’s still a lot of uncertainty about how much of this gas rush will come to fruition, so this future isn’t set in stone. Today, just 4.9 gigawatts of behind-the-meter gas projects tied to data centers are operating, and 15.8 gigawatts are under construction, according to Cleanview’s data.

Creative solutions could also help limit the climate burden of the on-site gas buildout, BloombergNEF’s Mishi says. Building gas alongside on-site renewables or energy storage could help limit how often a gas plant needs to fire up, she says, though the economics of building multiple energy sources can be tricky.

While the grid is struggling to keep up with demand, building more renewables could help, Fripp adds. In a recent study, his team found that building renewables and energy storage to meet rising electricity demand could be reliable and cheaper than relying on fossil fuels.

“These data centers want a lot of power, and they want it fast, and the grid is not well equipped to provide that,” Fripp says. “There are potentially good solutions and bad solutions … Rushing off the grid and putting in your own behind-the-meter gas is probably a bad way, because it’s still going to raise other people’s bills, and it’s not great for the environment.”
7b6b176c52e5d3b3: NOVEMBER 24 — The return of Jensen Huang to the helm of Nvidia has given the global artificial intelligence (AI) industry a much-needed psychological and financial boost.

Wall Street's strongest performance since April 2025, when President Donald Trump paused his Liberation Day tariffs, reflects the extraordinary importance of Nvidia to the contemporary global economy.

Yet the jubilation should not obscure the political, regulatory and economic challenges awaiting Nvidia and the wider AI industry. Huang may have returned, but the political environment in Washington is considerably less accommodating.
Nvidia’s centrality to the AI industry
Unlike many technology companies whose valuations are predicated on expectations of future earnings, Nvidia has been generating phenomenal revenues from the global expansion of AI infrastructure.

Its transformation from a supplier of graphics processors for gaming into an indispensable provider of advanced computing technologies is one of the most remarkable corporate achievements of the twenty-first century.

From Microsoft and Alphabet to Amazon and Meta, Nvidia has become a critical component of the technological ecosystem. Its importance extends beyond the United States, affecting Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Europe, China and Southeast Asia.
Huang’s return therefore represents more than the restoration of a corporate leader. It reassures an industry upon which trillions of dollars in investment increasingly depend.

Nevertheless, confidence in Nvidia should not be confused with confidence in the entire AI economy. The enormous expenditure on data centres, semiconductors and electricity infrastructure must eventually translate into sustainable commercial returns. Nvidia may remain profitable even if some of its largest customers struggle to monetise their AI investments.
Congress will not look the other way
The political backlash against Huang’s reinstatement is equally consequential.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren has described the decision as “reckless”, signalling that Nvidia could face extensive congressional scrutiny. Of particular significance is her determination to examine whether the company has fully complied with American export controls and whether senior Trump administration officials played a role in facilitating Huang's reinstatement.
These are legitimate questions of corporate governance and national security.

Even if the White House regards Nvidia as indispensable to American technological supremacy, this does not place the company beyond congressional oversight. Indeed, the greater Nvidia’s strategic importance, the stronger the argument for ensuring that its decisions remain transparent and consistent with American laws.

However, congressional scrutiny must not become an exercise in political persecution. Allegations of wrongdoing must be supported by credible evidence. The distinction between suspicion and proven misconduct remains fundamental to the integrity of American institutions.
The China dimension
At the heart of this controversy is Nvidia's commercial relationship with China.

Washington increasingly regards advanced AI semiconductors as strategic assets with implications for military computing, intelligence and technological competitiveness. This explains successive American efforts to restrict China’s access to sophisticated processors.
For Nvidia, however, China remains an important commercial market. The company must navigate between shareholder expectations and Washington’s national security priorities.
This is an increasingly difficult balancing act.

If export controls become excessively restrictive, China may accelerate its efforts to develop domestic alternatives, ultimately weakening American commercial influence. Conversely, relaxing restrictions without adequate safeguards could undermine Washington’s technological advantage.

The challenge is therefore not simply whether Nvidia should sell advanced chips to China. It is whether the United States can protect its national security interests without unnecessarily undermining its own technological competitiveness.
Huang’s return does not resolve this dilemma. If anything, it makes the debate more urgent.
Why Asean should pay attention

The implications extend well beyond Washington and Beijing. Nvidia's technological ecosystem depends on an intricate international supply chain, particularly the semiconductor manufacturing capabilities of Taiwan and South Korea, alongside Japan’s advanced semiconductor equipment and materials industries.
This interconnectedness means that any significant disruption to Nvidia’s operations could affect economies across the region.
For Asean, the lesson is particularly important.

Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia are increasingly positioning themselves as destinations for semiconductor investment, data centres and digital infrastructure. Malaysia, in particular, has sought to strengthen its position in semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging.

Yet attracting investment alone is insufficient. ASEAN must also develop domestic technological capabilities and ensure that its participation in the AI economy translates into meaningful economic value.

The Nvidia controversy demonstrates how technological interdependence can generate both opportunities and vulnerabilities. Companies operating across Southeast Asia may face increasingly complex compliance requirements as Washington tightens its export-control regime, particularly when their commercial activities involve China.

Asean should therefore avoid being drawn into a binary choice between Washington and Beijing. Its interests lie in maintaining an open, rules-based technological environment while strengthening regional cooperation in semiconductor supply chains, research and development, and export-control compliance.

Technological sovereignty does not mean isolation. It means possessing sufficient institutional capacity and strategic flexibility to make independent decisions amid intensifying geopolitical competition.
The real test lies ahead
Huang’s return is undoubtedly a victory for Nvidia’s investors, employees and business partners. But it should not be mistaken for the conclusion of the company’s difficulties.
Nvidia must still demonstrate that its commercial ambitions can coexist with regulatory compliance, corporate accountability and national security considerations.
For Congress, the responsibility is to scrutinise the company without undermining the innovation that has made the United States a global technology leader.
For Asean, the lesson is equally clear: the AI revolution must not become another arena in which Southeast Asian economies are merely consumers of technology developed elsewhere.

Huang’s return may have restored Wall Street’s confidence, but it has not settled the larger questions surrounding technological power, political accountability and the future of global semiconductor competition.
The celebration may be justified. The scrutiny, however, is equally necessary.

* Phar Kim Beng, PhD is the Professor of Asean Studies at International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS). Lutfy Hamzah is a research fellow at IITAS.** This is the personal opinion of the writers or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

311a6446282aa440: PETALING JAYA: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd’s (PCG) turnaround took a breather in the third quarter after it reported lower earnings from the preceding quarter amid softer overall average product prices.

The petrochemical group posted a net profit of RM179 million for the quarter ended Sept 30 (Q3 FY2026) from a net loss of RM289 million a year ago while revenue rose 12% to RM7.62 billion, according to its bourse filing today.

Net profit for the first nine months of FY2026 rose to RM994 million against a net loss of RM1.39 billion a year earlier when it booked foreign exchange losses and wrote down the value of assets at its Swedish specialty unit Perstorp.
Nine-month revenue was up nearly 8% year-on-year to RM22.54 billion as higher selling prices outweighed lower sales volumes and a stronger ringgit that cut into export receipts.

On a quarter-to-quarter basis, Q3 earnings were significantly lower as product prices fell, particularly for urea, a widely used fertiliser. Urea prices fell to US$407 per tonne from US$667 per tonne in the second quarter.

Profit after tax tumbled 54.6% to RM202 million from RM445 million in the second quarter. Third quarter revenue was down 4% to RM7.6 billion from the preceding quarter mainly due to lower average product prices despite higher sales volume from its Pengerang operations and strategic sourcing.

“The third quarter was marked by softer product prices across the portfolio, with urea particularly affected by increased export availability from China,” said managing director Mazuin Ismail in a statement.
Petronas Chemicals said its plants were operating at 73% of capacity in Q3, with utilisation reaching 90% in October following turnaround activities.
Its shares closed unchanged at RM3.82 today, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM30.56 billion. The stock is up 5.2% year to date.

Its shares surged nearly 105% to RM6.13 on March 30 after the US-Iran war ignited and Tehran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, driving up petroleum and petrochemical prices. The stock had been trading at RM3.00 just before the war started on Feb 28.

Petronas Chemicals was seen as a prime beneficiary of the crisis as it gets its feedstock supplies from within Malaysia rather than the Middle East. However, the stock has given up much of its gains in recent months.

The group is the chemical arm of national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and is one of Southeast Asia's largest integrated chemical producers. It operates 21 manufacturing sites and 54 production plants.

02f92d92c71694d5: For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. b289af96808c9563: SEREMBAN, Nov 24 — Three top Barisan Nasional (BN) leaders are expected to have an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here on Thursday, Sinar Harian reported.

Citing a source, the Malay daily said the three are BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, BN deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
“The purpose of the audience is to present the party’s decision reached at a special meeting at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan last Friday night.
“As far as we have been informed, Tuanku Muhriz has consented to receive them on that date, but it is not known whether it will be cancelled at the last minute,” the source was quoted as saying.
The source added that all BN state assemblymen had been instructed by the party not to issue any statements on the ongoing crisis to avoid worsening the situation.
However, the party is working to resolve the crisis, including the issue of the Menteri Besar, the source said.
Last Friday, 24 BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen in Negeri Sembilan agreed to abide by the directives of the top leadership in resolving the political impasse.
Sinar Harian reported that the decision was made after a special meeting at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan chaired by Mohamad.
It followed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s revelation that he had never agreed to his resignation letter, dated Nov 16, being submitted to Tuanku Muhriz.
The Juasseh assemblyman also said he had only learnt of the resignation, announced by the BN leadership, through media reports.
Since then, Ismail has not made any further statements, including in response to the Negeri Sembilan palace’s call for him to prove he has the support of a majority of assemblymen.
On Sunday, the Menteri Besar’s press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said Ismail was receiving treatment at a hospital here and that his condition was improving.
As of 3pm today, the media were still awaiting an update on Ismail’s condition, including whether he had been discharged, the daily reported.
892cd2519fde3b77: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur may not have enough weekends next year to accommodate the growing number of events and programmes planned for the capital, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh joked today.

She said the expansion of KL Festival and other creative programmes, supported by the government and private sector, would create more job opportunities while attracting domestic and international visitors.

“My only worry is we just don’t have enough weekends in 2027 to cater to all this. It’s a good problem for us in KL,” she told reporters after the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here.

Hannah said the festival’s second edition would run for 25 days, with support from the Federal Territories Ministry, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Finance Ministry, adding that she expected a bigger crowd than this year.
She said organisers were also looking to expand activities beyond the annual festival through year-round programmes, including concerts and events at public parks.

Think City, which is involved in organising the festival, said its pilot events last year generated more than 1,400 job opportunities, with the figure expected to double annually as the creative sector expands.
Hannah said the growing number of programmes would give young people more opportunities to showcase their talents and find employment.

She also cited the entertainment tax incentives announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027 in Parliament, alongside Visit Malaysia Year, as factors that would contribute to a busy year for Kuala Lumpur.

“KL Festival cannot happen without the support of the private sector. And with Visit Malaysia Year coming back a second year and together with this entertainment tax incentive that the Prime Minister has announced for Budget 2027, I believe it will be a busy 12 months in Kuala Lumpur,” she said.
63f90f482b3d4aaa: InferNode brings a modernized, 64-bit edition of Inferno, the distributed operating system that followed Plan 9 from Bell Labs.

For us, the strapline of the InferNode project distracts from the interesting part. It describes the project as a "Secure Runtime for AI Agents," but we think it's something far more interesting than another LLM tool.

Fair warning: this vulture has no interest whatsoever in AI agents, and we are not even going to look at this planned use of InferNode. We're interested in the OS, and here, its GitHub repository spells out the part that caught our attention: "a 64-bit Inferno® OS."
That grabbed us because Inferno is a very interesting OS, although it doesn't get much attention – for example, the official Inferno GitHub repository shows little activity in the last few years.
Inferno is the successor to Plan 9, which we've written and talked about before, including recent releases of its community continuation, 9front.

Plan 9 is what the team who invented Unix did next. Plan 9 is a very minimalist, natively clustered Unix: machines can freely mount one another's filesystems, display windows on one another, and start processes on one another. Plan 9 turns a network of machines running this Unix-like OS into a single machine. So, for instance, if you were working on a laptop with limited storage and compute power, you could compile a large complex project on a faster machine elsewhere on the network, using project files located on a third machine, while watching the process in your terminal on your screen, with no messing about with SSH sessions.

Plan 9 and 9front programs are compiled into architecture-specific native binaries. Different processor families can still work together across the network, but the same executable won't run unchanged on both an x86-64 laptop and an Arm64 server.

Inferno takes a different approach. It's contemporaneous with the far less ambitious Java. On Inferno, languages compile code for a VM called Dis, which is part of the kernel. This means that Inferno binaries execute directly on anything that the Inferno kernel runs on. The OS kernel is built to run bare-metal, or as a process on various other OSes, without needing a separate hardware virtual machine or hypervisor.

A single binary can run on all supported CPU architectures. Inferno applications are normally written in the Limbo programming language, whose documentation was written by Unix co-creator Dennis Ritchie. Limbo is one of the languages that influenced Go, but Inferno lets compilers for other languages target Dis as well. The binaries run anywhere. Inferno on Arm, or x86, or RISC-V, or running in a Windows or Linux or macOS process, your program just runs.

We've been trying to contact Vita Nuova, the company that maintains Inferno, for some years without success. Development appears to have slowed considerably. Moving the runtime to 64-bit also raises compatibility questions: some forks change Dis's word size and cannot run existing 32-bit bytecode unchanged.

We're aware of several efforts to build 64-bit versions of Inferno. Caerwyn Jones's Inferno64 is one of the more visible, and the GitHub repository (and indeed his X account) show considerable activity. However, Inferno64's Dis is not compatible with 32-bit Dis code. Another fork is Dinsmoor's Inferno64, which also shows recent activity, albeit with the assistance of the Claude LLM. Others include the long-quiescent Purgatorio and 9ferno, both inactive for years, plus Scott Guyon's more active fork. Dropping the compatibility goal altogether, Node9 replaces Limbo with Lua and Dis with LuaJIT.

There are more forks and variants than we've gone into here. Given that there have been quite a few efforts, and most haven't delivered final ready-to-use products yet, we were surprised when InferNode was suddenly announced on the Inferno-OS mailing list last week.

Developer Peter Finn said: "An experimental runtime for containing generative AI agents was the original motivation, but most of the work since has been on the OS itself, and the AI parts are ordinary file servers. For example, llmsrv at /mnt/llm and speech9p are started from the login profile, and if you delete those lines they're simply not there. There's also non-generative AI additions on object detection served as files at /mnt/vision, on the CPU or a GPU host, and voice calls between devices done by mounting each other's audio files over 9P. There's a GUI layer intended to facilitate hands-free AI agent use, but it too is optional."

He also said that InferNode's development was largely independent of the existing efforts, partly because the primary target was Arm64, not x86-64. Its 64-bit Dis runtime is incompatible with the 32-bit original: "The opcodes, file format and magic number are unchanged, but the word size isn't, so frame sizes, offsets and pointer maps all differ. Limbo source recompiles without edits. A 32-bit .dis is currently rejected at load time."

InferNode doesn't implement 9front's DP9IK authentication protocol, so it cannot connect to servers requiring that authentication. Dr Finn told us: "DP9IK is not quantum-safe. That's the reason. InferNode's current crypto policy is strict CNSA."

InferNode also includes some slightly unexpected components, related to its intended use for testing LLM agents – such as a wallet for the Ethereum cryptocurrency, which Finn said was "mainly to support agent payments."

The first release of Inferno was in 1996, the year after Java and the JVM were launched. Inferno is a much more ambitious project, but its core function – the ability to run identical binaries on multiple platforms, without recompilation – was close enough that they ended up competing in the market, and Java won. It was a pleasant surprise to see a modernized version of Inferno arrive this year, 30 years on.

Finn told us: "About a year ago I saw the potential for a 'break-out' moment for this tech as a runtime for containing AI agents. The flood of cybersecurity risks we would face on account of adversarial AI agents required new systems with small footprints and minimal attack surfaces. Inferno was a perfect candidate and it was an opportunity to show the world how visionary Plan 9's ideas were and how well they mapped on to pressing contemporary security issues."
"If InferNode succeeds, it is an opportunity for Plan 9's ideas to migrate out of hobby-land and really make an impact – as they deservedly should."

He has a point. On a related note, this vulture discussed the possibility of rebuilding the world's IT systems from scratch on last week's Kettle podcast. Perhaps the hour for tools like this really has come round at last. ®
86834d45dd3e12d2: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur’s heritage landmarks have the potential to become international tourist attractions, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said, pointing to the positive public response to French President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit to the capital.

She said Macron’s walkabout through the city, including his appearance at Dataran Merdeka with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building as a backdrop, showed how Kuala Lumpur’s historic sites could help shape its appeal to international visitors.
“We could have taken him to one of our newest and tallest buildings, and the new condominium, but we took him to Dataran Merdeka with the Sultan Abdul Samad building behind it.

“I think that choice says something about how we want the world to see Kuala Lumpur. Since the inspection and the pictures went viral, we have received a lot of feedback from people. They said, what an amazing idea to take him to the Sultan Abdul Samad Building,” she said in her speech at the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here today.
Hannah said the city’s heritage should be preserved while its public spaces are made more accessible and inviting, allowing both residents and visitors to experience its history.

“When people talk about Kuala Lumpur, when people talk about the inspection of world leaders, it’s no longer just pictures in Putrajaya, but they see Pasar Seni, Medan Pasar, and all other parts of Kuala Lumpur,” she said.
She also defended the RM600 million restoration of the Sultan Abdul Samad Building, saying the work was now showing results.
Her remarks came as she announced the return of KL Festival for its third edition, which will run from May 6 to 30 next year under the theme “Bridges of Belonging”.

The festival will feature activities across downtown Kuala Lumpur, including the Dataran Merdeka Heritage Area, Masjid Jamek, Central Market and Petaling Street, with satellite events planned for Brickfields and Kampung Baru.
Hannah said initiatives such as the festival could help bring heritage spaces to life through cultural programmes and activities, while giving younger generations a greater role in shaping the city.
She said Kuala Lumpur should continue developing without losing its identity, adding that its heritage and public spaces could help give visitors reasons to return and explore.
8131104559aaa680: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — KL Festival will return to Downtown Kuala Lumpur from May 6 to 30 next year, with Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh hoping to turn the capital into a more attractive destination through cultural events and unconventional tourism offerings.

Themed “Bridges of Belonging”, the 25-day festival will feature performances, exhibitions and community activities across the city’s historic core, from the Dataran Merdeka Heritage Area to Central Market and Petaling Street, with satellite programmes in Brickfields and Kampung Baru.
“I think that what makes Kuala Lumpur important is that it gives people a reason to come back to explore,” Hannah said at the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here today.

She said Kuala Lumpur needed to explore new attractions that could appeal to different groups of visitors, including younger tourists, rather than relying solely on conventional sightseeing and shopping experiences.

Hannah recounted how she had taken her two daughters to Pasar Seni after they expressed an interest in buying Squishies, a popular collectible among young people, instead of visiting heritage attractions.
She also recalled asking a French official accompanying French President Emmanuel Macron during his visit to Kuala Lumpur last week whether he had time to explore the city.
“He said he didn’t have time because he had a meeting, but his daughter in France told him to buy something from KL for her. Guess what? A Squishy,” she said.
Hannah said the experience showed how popular culture and the interests of younger generations could create new opportunities for Kuala Lumpur’s tourism industry.

She also suggested developing themed shopping destinations, including dedicated areas for watches and perfumes, so visitors could find specialised products in one location rather than having to visit multiple places.
She said such initiatives could give tourists more reasons to return to Kuala Lumpur and explore different parts of the city.

The 2026 edition of KL Festival attracted 140,000 visitors and recorded more than 100,000 attendances, while generating more than 1,400 jobs and gigs for artists, producers, designers and crew members, according to the organisers.

Hannah said the festival’s impact should extend beyond its annual run, with the government working alongside Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Think City and the private sector to sustain cultural activities throughout the year.

“The government is behind Kuala Lumpur and we will not let Think City go it alone,” she said, urging businesses and financial institutions to support the festival through sponsorships and partnerships.
She said the creative sector could also provide more employment opportunities for young people, particularly those with skills and ideas that might otherwise have limited avenues to be showcased.
“Without events and programmes, there’ll be very little opportunity for young people with creative ideas to showcase their talent and to be hired for these kind of roles,” she said.

Think City, which organises the festival alongside DBKL with support from the Finance Ministry and the Federal Territories Department, said it had outlined a five-year roadmap to establish KL Festival as a flagship event while progressively introducing year-round activities.

Its representative said the more than 1,400 jobs and gigs generated through the 2026 edition were expected to grow, with the organisation aiming for creative-sector employment opportunities to double annually.

Among the first confirmed highlights for next year’s festival are Jogeton, a community dance celebration featuring a new segment for children, and Gema Kuala Lumpur, which will feature two all-women dikir barat performances along the River of Life.

Other programmes include Our Love Song, a musical theatre production exploring stories behind Malaysia’s national identity, including the national anthem Negaraku, and Songs of the Bulbul by British South Asian dancer Aakash Odedra.

The line-up will also feature Efectos Especiales, a free street performance from Argentina, the world premiere of HuRU-hARa: nUSaNtAra, a collaborative production involving artists from Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia and Timor-Leste, and KataRaya: KL Festival Literature Week.

Other public programmes include KL Discovery Race, a citywide treasure hunt, KL Frozen in Time, a collective photography project, KL Builds, which invites participants to recreate city landmarks using recycled materials, and KL Beat: The City Marches, a procession involving drummers and marching groups from across Kuala Lumpur.

Most festival activities will be free, while ticketed performances will be priced to keep the arts accessible. Its Pay It Forward initiative will also extend access to residents of People’s Housing Projects (PPR), schools, senior citizens’ homes and children’s homes.
More programme details, venues and ticketing information will be announced ahead of the festival.
729cb52e6dbbfd37: SHAH ALAM, Nov 24 — The Selangor state government is prepared to obtain a loan from the Federal Government if necessary to accelerate the implementation of flood mitigation projects, including resolving drainage system problems at the local authority level.

Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the move reflects the state government’s commitment to ensuring that flooding issues, particularly flash floods that frequently occur in urban areas, can be addressed more comprehensively.

“Given that the state government currently has no outstanding loans from the Federal Government, I believe that whether the amount is tens of millions or billions of ringgit, I think it is worth it for the state government to take out a loan to resolve these drainage problems, including those at the local authority level,” he said during the winding-up session of the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates debate at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.

Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government has also allocated RM100 million for flood mitigation purposes next year, almost double the allocation made in 2022, and it is prepared to bear additional expenses to ensure that related projects can be implemented without being overly constrained by financial limitations.

Local authorities have also been directed to allocate between 20 and 30 per cent of their respective reserves specifically for flood management, in order to strengthen urban areas’ resilience against the risks posed by changing weather patterns, he said.

“Another issue that I believe needs to be emphasised is the coordination of efforts, monitoring and communication among all agencies, so that they work together as one team to address the flooding issue,” Amirudin said.

On a related development, he said flooding in the Parit Mahang area of Ijok was caused not only by overflowing water but also by a slow drainage system due to culvert structures in front of houses, as well as incidents of broken embankments and high-tide phenomena.
He said water-pumping operations in Parit Mahang could only begin 20 days after the flooding occurred, as the high tide levels beforehand had rendered pumping efforts ineffective.
“The pumped water is channelled directly into rivers or the sea to help reduce water accumulation in the affected areas,” he said.
He also shared that the process of acquiring land used as an illegal dumping site in the Ijok area is expected to be completed around March 2027. — Bernama
993a246d7a6954b7: BALI, Nov 24 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that differences in political views and positions among parties forming the Federal Government do not affect the country’s administration.
Ahmad Zahid, also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said political maturity enabled party leaders to put aside their differences when carrying out their shared responsibility of governing the country.

“When it comes to administering the government, we set aside those differences. When discussing matters concerning national interests, we remain highly professional, and there are no disagreements,” he told Bernama here today.

He was responding to questions about the Amanah 2026 National Convention held last Sunday, where delegates passed a motion, with the support of nearly all attendees, for the party to contest the 16th General Election (GE16) without cooperating with BN.

However, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu was reported to have clarified that the resolution was merely a recommendation by the party to be submitted to the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council, with any final decision on electoral cooperation to be made at the coalition level.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, arrived in Bali on Monday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, involving a series of official engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
He is scheduled to depart for Jakarta today. — Bernama
1dd18e81ee97d983: The British government is investing in a UK-based AI defense startup that aims to train autonomous military systems in virtual environments, in a bid to reduce the country's reliance on overseas technology.
Both the Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) have contributed to a Series A funding round for Agon Dynamics, said to value the biz at $450 million.
This $70 million round takes the total capital raised by the firm to $100 million, following its initial $30 million seed round earlier this year.

The government claims this move will help strengthen the UK’s sovereign capabilities when it comes to the use of AI for defense, plus the hope that nurturing native technical know-how converts into industrial strength and greater resilience.

But it is not revealing how much cash it has stumped up, claiming such investments are commercially sensitive, although it did say that typical equity amounts obtained from the the Sovereign AI Fund tend to be worth around £1 million to £10 million ($1.3 million to $13 million).

Agon is understood to be developing facilities to train and test AI systems needed for defense. This covers systems to help defend against drone attacks, or ensuring that AI tools still continue to work as intended if communications with the command center are disrupted.

Training like this currently needs to be carried out in the real world, which is time-consuming and expensive, according to the government. For this reason, Agon is building a "virtual battlefield" environment where AI models can be tested against realistic simulations of the situations they might encounter.

The company says its synthetic battle arena provides a safe, repeatable environment for developers and defense contractors to try out autonomous systems against thousands of demanding scenarios before deployment. Systems can face adaptive virtual adversaries informed by live conflict intelligence, helping them to respond to evolving tactics, threats and operating conditions.

This may include simulations of mass drone attacks that would overwhelm conventional air defense systems, or testing how autonomous systems operate when navigation is degraded or adversary tactics change.

"Europe is in an AI arms race as we enter the era of agentic warfare: intelligent agents and machines that will need to understand their environment, make decisions and adapt at a speed and scale that humans alone cannot match," says co-founder and CEO Tristam Constant, a former British Army officer.

"We exist to build the sovereign infrastructure and AI foundation models to allow us to train, test, and evolve autonomous defense systems, in Europe, for Europe - to outperform adversary capabilities."
For the government, AI Minister Kanishka Narayan claimed that Britain is well-placed to lead efforts to ensure such technologies are reliable, trustworthy, and deployed responsibly.

"AI is rapidly transforming how wars are fought, from the use of drones through to how rapidly soldiers can interpret battlefield information. The UK needs sovereign defence AI capabilities to bolster our national security in this new era," he stated. ®
c9b64772c5cd353a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Indian music sensation HipHop Tamizha Adhi is returning to Malaysia with his new world tour, Mirugam Mode (Beast Mode), which kicks off at Stadium Merdeka here on March 27, 2027.
Malaysia was chosen as the first stop of the tour, which carries the tagline “Malaysia first. Then the world.”
The concert is organised by Don’t Run Away Asia and marks a new chapter for the artist. His previous Malaysian concert drew a crowd of about 30,000 fans.
Adhi is returning with a bigger vision and a completely reimagined live show, which the organisers say will push the boundaries of live entertainment.
A beast of a concert
Mirugam Mode promises an immersive, high-energy experience featuring state-of-the-art production, cutting-edge visuals, spectacular lighting, innovative stage technology and special effects.

The organisers said the show would bring together music, technology and electrifying performances, with special guest appearances and surprise elements still under wraps. More announcements are expected as the concert draws closer.

Adhi’s fan community, known as the HHT Troop, has been instrumental in shaping his journey. Following the overwhelming response to his last concert here, the organisers are calling on fans to reunite and bring their signature energy to the show, which they describe as a movement driven by music, unity and the passion of its fans.

Don’t Run Away Asia, led by Datuk Ramesh Arumugam and Al Muzammil, said opening the tour in Malaysia would help position the country as a key destination for international live entertainment, while creating opportunities to take the Mirugam Mode experience to audiences around the world.

“Bringing Mirugam Mode to Malaysia as the opening destination of the world tour is something we are incredibly proud of. Following the overwhelming response to HipHop Tamizha’s previous concert, we wanted to return with something bigger, bolder and more immersive for the fans.
“This is more than just a concert; it is about creating an unforgettable experience that celebrates the music, the energy and the incredible connection between the artist and his fans.

“We are excited to bring this vision to life at Stadium Merdeka and hope the HHT Troop will come together once again to make history. Malaysia is where it begins, and the world comes next,” Ramesh said.

Al Muzammil said Malaysia had always had the potential to be a major destination for international entertainment, and the organisers were committed to playing their part in strengthening that position.
“Bringing Mirugam Mode to Stadium Merdeka as the first stop of the world tour is a significant milestone, not just for us as organisers, but also for the local live entertainment industry.

“Our ambition is to deliver world-class concert experiences while giving Malaysian fans access to productions of an international standard. We hope this event will demonstrate what Malaysia can offer on the global entertainment stage and set the tone for even bigger opportunities ahead,” he said.
72-hour fan sale
As a token of appreciation to fans who made the previous concert a success, the organisers will hold an exclusive 72-hour fan sale with specially discounted tickets in limited numbers.
The fan sale starts on Nov 27 and runs for 72 hours or until the allocated tickets sell out, whichever comes first.
Early bird ticket sales will then begin on Nov 30.
Tickets are available via Ticket2U at https://www.ticket2u.com.my/hiphoptamizha27.
2943f371348fc857: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 24 — Malaysians can now renew their passports through the MyGov Malaysia app, including submitting applications, making online payments and selecting an Immigration Department office for passport collection.
In a statement today, the Digital Ministry said the enhanced MyGov Malaysia app version 2.1.4 allows the public to manage applications digitally with greater ease and speed.
According to the statement, the facility is among the key improvements introduced by GovTech Malaysia to strengthen the digitalisation of public services.

“In the initial phase, the passport collection facility is available only at the Shaftsbury Immigration Office in Putrajaya. Other collection locations will be expanded in stages to improve access and convenience for the public nationwide,” the statement said.
Besides passport renewal, the ministry said the app also enhances the MyNotifikasi function with more targeted, personalised notification delivery according to user needs.

The improvements let the public receive announcements, programme information, initiatives and important notices from ministries, departments and agencies directly through the app, so Malaysians do not miss service and initiative information relevant to them.
“MyGov Malaysia also introduces a function to check the location of National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) under the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.

“This function makes it easier for the public to identify nearby Nadi centres to access various facilities and programmes provided free of charge, including internet access, health checks and the Tuisyen Rakyat programme,” the statement said.
The ministry said the initiative also supports the expansion of digital access, improves digital literacy and strengthens learning opportunities among local communities.
The public are therefore encouraged to update the MyGov Malaysia app to the latest version via the Apple App Store, Google Play Store and Huawei AppGallery to enjoy the latest features.

“The Madani government will continue to strengthen the digital services ecosystem through cross-ministry and agency cooperation to deliver more efficient, integrated and people-centric government services, in line with Malaysia’s aspiration towards an AI Nation by 2030,” the statement said. — Bernama
d88deea5cf9b839d: VILLAVICENCIO, Nov 24 — A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio yesterday destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said.
The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years.
"They have just carried out a bombing attack on the Meta Governor's Office," De la Espriella said in a post on X, referring to Colombia's central province of Meta.
The president said there were no casualties confirmed.
Around twenty people were injured, according to local media reports.
Following the blast, residents sought shelter in nearby streets strewn with the wreckage of damaged buildings, rubble and a visible large crater, AFP journalists saw.
Johan Perez said the blast damaged his hat shop, and "the doors were bent in, the windows shattered, some display cases inside broken."
"We are alive by a miracle," he told AFP.
De la Espriella said the attack was carried out by drug traffickers.
"I warn the narco-terrorists responsible: you will answer for every drop of blood you have spilled and every business and property you have destroyed," he said.
"We will deploy the full power of the state to hunt you down, dismantle your organizations and take you out."
Ombudsman Iris Marin called the incident "unacceptable and painful."
"Instilling fear is easy. Building, rebuilding -- that takes courage," she said on X.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Anniversary of peace agreement
Yesterday's attack coincided with the eve of the tenth anniversary of the signing of the peace agreement between the Colombian state and the FARC.

The deal ended FARC's brutal campaign of bombings, assassinations and hostage-takings, but violence has flared again over the past two years as remaining guerrilla groups and cartels vie for control of the cocaine trade, illegal gold mines and extortion rackets.
The country, which is the world's largest producer of cocaine, is now facing its worst wave of criminal violence in a decade.

US-backed De la Espriella is a critic of the past peace process, arguing that FARC fighters got off too lightly -- they were spared prison in return for admitting to their crimes -- fostering what he sees as a culture of impunity.
Minutes before the blast, the president criticized the "false peace" deal in a post on X.
"False peace, the squandering of public resources, and corruption scandals during Petro's administration are what have brought Colombia to ruin," he said.
De la Espriella has vowed to put all remaining armed groups, including breakaway FARC factions, "in a tomb or in prison" and stepped up bombardments of their positions. — AFP
d3f50cd2bd995396: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Lawyers representing comedian Harith Iskander in a defamation suit brought by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor have been unable to contact him despite repeated attempts, prompting the High Court today to defer their application to withdraw from the case until December 4.

High Court judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi set the new date after Harith failed to attend today’s proceedings, directing his lawyers to make further reasonable efforts to ensure he appeared in person on that date or, at the very least, provided a reasonable response, Utusan Malaysia reported.
“Until the defendant appears, I cannot allow Enclosure 15 (the application to withdraw).
“I will give one final date. Make every reasonable effort, and the court can then make an appropriate order on Enclosure 15,” she said, as reported by the national daily.
Lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo told the court that attempts to serve notice on Harith had been made through email, WhatsApp and visits to his home.

During the first attempt to serve notice at his home, the document was received by his domestic helper as Harith was not there. A subsequent letter seeking to arrange an appointment was also accepted by the helper.
“But when we returned to serve the notice on that date, neither the helper nor Harith Iskander was there. We were not allowed into the residential area,” Sangeet said.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, she said her legal team had yet to receive instructions from the comedian despite repeated attempts.
“We have made numerous attempts but have yet to obtain any instructions. So, I hope to receive a response from him,” she was quoted as saying.
Sangeet appeared alongside Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh, while Rosmah was represented by Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.

Rosmah, 74, filed the defamation suit against Harith, 60, on June 9, alleging that he had ridiculed her physical appearance during a stand-up comedy show, Harith Iskander: The Outspoken Comedy Tour, on January 17.

She alleged that Harith had displayed an image of a frightening mythical creature before showing an image of her, and had made mocking remarks about looking in the rear-view mirror while driving along a dark road.

Rosmah claimed that footage of the performance, subsequently uploaded by a TikTok user and viewed hundreds of thousands of times, had damaged her reputation and dignity as a public figure and patron of charitable organisations.
In his statement of defence filed on July 9, Harith denied that the material carried the defamatory meaning alleged by Rosmah.

7315e960f6bc4f8a: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September.

The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen.

As The Register reported in October, the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it.

Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on.
Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server.

The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems.

Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach.

Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make.

As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins.
The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess.
The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response.
Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®
